scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring ticket #9127: I'm covering the monitoring desk today and part of
the network has gone missing from the screens after one of the boxes was
restarted. The senior people are clear about what happened: the two parts
were joined by something called a "virtual link", and traffic trying to cross
it now just disappears. I won't pretend I know what a virtual link is -- that
is your area, not mine. What I can see is that the far part is unreachable,
and it went missing right after that restart, so this is on your side. Check
how the two parts are joined and reconnect them today, please.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF virtual-links are intact: r4 and r8
  both hold their `area 1 virtual-link` config, the virtual adjacency is up, and
  every non-backbone area remains attached to Area 0. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss, exercising a path that depends on the
  converged multi-area fabric. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of a virtual-link collapse that is not occurring (cf.
  kath5-r4-virtual-link-removed / kath5-r8-virtual-link-removed, where one IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a collapsed OSPF
virtual-link leaving an area unreachable -- is NOT reproducible: the r4<->r8
virtual adjacency is up (both endpoints still configure `area 1 virtual-link`,
each pointing at the other's router-id), and the transit chain stitching the
non-backbone areas to Area 0 is intact. End-to-end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
(120.1.1.10) with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone + virtual-links + the EIGRP
domain, which it could not if a virtual-link on the path had collapsed.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the virtual-links are up and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks the virtual-link state
(both endpoints present, adjacency up), confirms the affected area's prefixes are
still in the RIB, and exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all healthy -- and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a collapsed virtual-link or a stranded area --
blaming r4/r8 or re-adding a virtual-link that is already there -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text: A thorough inspection of all topology layers reveals no active fault. The OSPF virtual link between r4 and r8 — the specific component the monitoring ticket describes — is fully operational: both endpoints show a Full OSPF adjacency on VLINK0 (r4 sees 18.1.4.1/Full, r8 sees 14.1.4.1/Full), and area 0.0.0.2 routes (18.1.x.x/32 loopbacks and 80.0.0.0/8) are correctly installed in r1's routing table via the r3→r4→VLINK0→r8 path. The OSPF helper flagged r8's area 0.0.0.2 as "orphaned" because it has zero OSPF adjacencies across its five active interfaces, but this is the intended stub-ABR design: all five interfaces are loopbacks or the single-device BB stub segment, where adjacencies are architecturally impossible. The helper flag is a false positive. The EIGRP/OSPF redistribution domain is also healthy: eigrpd runs on r11, r12, and r13; r11 has Full EIGRP neighbors on both its 112.0.0.0/8 (r12) and 103.0.0.0/8 (r13) segments; and r13's four loopback prefixes (113.1.x.0/24) are redistributed into OSPF at r11 and visible on r1. The "far part went missing after a restart" describes a transient OSPF reconvergence window: when a router restarted, the virtual link dropped and required roughly one dead-interval (~40 s) to re-establish. No flap script, no misconfigured interface, no wrong area assignment, and no daemon outage that persists today. The current state is fully converged and healthy; no corrective action is required.

per_axis.rationale: Agent confirms the r4↔r8 virtual-link is up but does not explicitly confirm end-to-end PC0→PC12 reachability across the multi-area fabric as required.

The agent gathered host-level reachability, control-plane snapshots, neighbor outputs, and routing tables that largely support ‘no fault’. There is a minor inconsistency in the r8 neighbor evidence (helper vs. direct vtysh output), but the presence of r4's VLINK adjacency, the OSPF-learned prefixes in r1's RIB, and successful end-to-end probes justify the conclusion.
